name: Cheap Trick
description:
'''Cheap Trick''' is an American rock band formed in [[Rockford, Illinois]], in 1973. The band's work bridged elements of 1960s guitar pop, 1970s [[hard rock]], and the emerging [[punk rock]] sound, and helped set the template for subsequent [[power pop]] artists.

Cheap Trick released its [[Cheap Trick (1977 album)|self-titled debut album]] in 1977. Later that year, the band found success in Japan with the release of its second album, ''[[In Color (Cheap Trick album)|In Color]]''. In 1979, the band released the [[RIAA certification|triple-platinum]] live album ''[[Cheap Trick at Budokan|At Budokan]]'' and a Top 10 single, a live recording of "[[I Want You to Want Me]]". The band followed with its most commercially successful studio album, ''[[Dream Police]]'' (1979), which reached No. 6 on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] chart. After experiencing declining popularity in the 1980s, Cheap Trick enjoyed a major resurgence toward the end of the decade, topping the US charts with the [[power ballad]] "[[The Flame (Cheap Trick song)|The Flame]]" (from 1988's ''[[Lap of Luxury]]''). The band's other hits include "[[Surrender (Cheap Trick song)|Surrender]]" (1978), "[[Dream Police (song)|Dream Police]]" (1979), "[[Voices (Cheap Trick song)|Voices]]" (1979), "[[She's Tight]]" (1982), "[[Tonight It's You]]" (1985), a cover version of [[Elvis Presley]]'s "[[Don't Be Cruel]]" (1988), "[[Ghost Town (Cheap Trick song)|Ghost Town]]" (1988), and "[[Can't Stop Fallin' into Love]]" (1990).

Cheap Trick has continued releasing new music into the 21st century. The band has performed live more than 5,000 times since its formation and has sold more than 20 million albums. The band's influence has been cited by a diverse range of rock artists. Cheap Trick was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2016.
